approval.notes: April Act 1 gate beat; the hill gates are wooden and the exchange stays on the All-linn/Domberg boundary.

nodes.text: The All-linn watch is drawing the wooden leaves of Pikk jalg and Lühike jalg. When the hill-gate curfew is called, Domberg keeps its messengers above us and the council keeps the stairs below. Carry the report now, or wait for daylight.

choices.text: I will not test the chain tonight.

nodes.text: Wait below the gate line. The watch closes the route from the Lower Town side after dark; a hill clerk may speak of Domberg, but no message crosses these stairs until the chain is lifted.

source_notes.summary: The dialogue uses the dossier's April distinction between Toompea/Domberg and All-linn and its two named hill-gate routes.
A short courier exchange turns the documented wooden-gate curfew seam into an authored Act 1 beat without activating a map or assigning new historical characters.
